method: Differences of cumulative per-vehicle timeLoss between route-specific local entry and exit boundaries. Passive subscriptions do not alter the original inputs or decision rule.
entry_truncation: At network origin or previous signal. Vehicles born inside an area are tracked from actual insertion with initial timeLoss zero.
exit_truncation: At available outgoing-edge end or actual route end; exact boundaries retained for every route.
aggregation: Within each run, volume-weight all completed local passage time losses at each site. Report run-level means and sample SD across seeds; map the reported mean to signalized LOS delay thresholds.
open_passages: Retain every entered but unfinished local passage and its accumulated loss; not inserted demand remains in the original all-demand ledger.
reproduction_acceptance: Existing accepted journey, completion, active, uninserted, collision and teleport results must match; every completed trip visiting a target approach must have a local passage record.
classification_scope: Simulation-based bounded-area LOS estimate only, not an independently field-calibrated HCM capacity analysis.
limitations: Sub-step boundary interpolation is approximate; source-born and route-ending vehicles use insertion/arrival counters.
Time loss can include non-signal interaction and junction geometry; truncated areas can omit external queues or acceleration.
LOS of cleared local passages does not include vehicles unable to enter or clear the measured area.
Do not average grades or infer a corridor LOS from network travel time.
